delta.comment: Stage readiness-fix cycle 3 of 3 (shipment 143-S / feature 134-F): corrected blocking P1 — the mandatory out-of-scope disposition sequence required a PR/review-thread ID, thread reply, and thread resolution for EVERY finding, which is unsatisfiable for Ship's pre-PR local-review findings (local review runs before PR creation) and for threadless build/CI findings. Acceptance criteria now split the disposition into a common mandatory CAPTURE-FIRST step (a) plus two continuation paths: THREAD-PRESENT (record PR/thread IDs -> substantive reply citing the generated deferred entry ID per C3 -> resolve thread -> PR/closure residual-risk record) and THREADLESS (PR and review-thread payload fields recorded explicitly NOT APPLICABLE; deferred entry ID cited in task/run/closure residual-risk records; no reply or resolution required or possible, and their absence is not a C3 shortfall). Path selection is driven by whether a thread actually exists for the finding, not by which loop raised it; a threadless-captured finding that later reaches a PR thread reuses the already-captured entry ID rather than generating a second entry. C2 is not relaxed on either path — both preserve the full six-field capture payload, the C1-cited out-of-scope rationale, and the provisional-priority / Stage-only reprioritization rule. Description item 2 and implementation notes updated with the correction record. TARGETED CONSISTENCY CHECK vs corrected 134.006-T and 134.007-T: 134.007-T already distinguishes the threadless fix-ci path and uses the same disposition — aligned, no change needed. 134.006-T covers the github-pr-automation PR comment loop where a thread always exists, so its single capture-first sequence and its consistency clause naming this task both map to this task's THREAD-PRESENT path — scope-of-applicability difference, not an ordering divergence; no change needed. Six-field payload, C1 rationale, and Stage-only reprioritization verified present on all three surfaces. backlogit_doctor target validation: pass. Stage-owned backlog artifact edit only; no template/source/config mutation, no shipment claim, no build, no PR/merge. Changes left uncommitted for Orchestrator.

Staging-readiness remediation (2026-08-19, P1 contract fix). The thread-present path previously mandated recording the PR number and review-thread ID in the captured entry AFTER the C2 capture. That is unsatisfiable: the C5 capture-only carve-out (134.002-T/134.003-T) grants Ship entry CREATION only and forbids editing a captured entry, so the mandated back-fill would have been a P-010 violation at execution time. Corrected under a SINGLE-WRITE CAPTURE INVARIANT: the C2 capture is Ship's only write; all source IDs known at capture are recorded at capture, unavailable fields as explicit N/A; the thread-present path now has no write-back step; a late-surfacing thread cites the existing deferred entry ID in the reply and the Ship-owned residual-risk record without editing or duplicating the entry, with reconciliation left to Stage under C6. Preserved unchanged: six-field payload, C1-cited rationale, capture-first ordering, provisional-priority / Stage-only reprioritization. Cross-surface re-verified: 134.006-T and 134.007-T already populate source refs at capture and needed no change, so this brings 004 into agreement with its siblings.

Stage fix cycle 1 (2026-08-19, current-HEAD review of 0facdf01, P1). The threadless path mandated BOTH the PR number and the review-thread ID as N/A in a single blanket pairing. That is wrong for build/CI findings: fix-ci runs against an OPEN PR, so the PR number is known at capture and only the thread ID is genuinely unavailable. Because the SINGLE-WRITE CAPTURE INVARIANT forbids supplying the value later, marking a known PR number N/A would have permanently discarded a real identifier, contradicting this task's own criterion (4) and diverging from 134.007-T, which marks only the review-thread ID not applicable and never the PR number. Corrected to evaluate source-ref availability INDEPENDENTLY PER FIELD: review-thread ID is N/A whenever no thread exists; the PR number carries its actual value whenever a PR is open and is N/A only for a genuinely pre-PR finding; both are N/A together only in that pre-PR case. Added a dedicated criterion stating N/A is a per-field availability marker and never a path-level default, and removed the both-fields-N/A presumption from the late-surfacing-thread criterion. Preserved: capture-first ordering, six-field payload, C1-cited rationale, single-write invariant, provisional-priority / Stage-only reprioritization. Cross-surface re-verified: 134.006-T (PR and thread always concrete) and 134.007-T (only thread ID N/A) both remain clean and unchanged; this brings 004 into agreement with 007.

Correction cycle 2 (HEAD 663205a6): C3 symmetric guard expanded to its complete TWO-PART authoritative form -- (i) a same-contract-surface completion of the authorized change IS in scope and must be fixed, not deferred; AND (ii) deferring one without a captured deferred entry and a residual-risk record is itself a P-021 violation, actioned per C7. This task previously carried only part (i), which forbids under-fixing but leaves silent deferral unpenalized -- part (ii) is what makes the guard SYMMETRIC. The B9 semantic test in 134.012-T already required both parts, so this task's contract was under-specified relative to the test that asserts it. No change to C2/C3/C7 semantics, no new obligation on paths this surface does not handle.

PR #372 Copilot review-fix cycle 1 — thread PRRT_kwDORzpWpM6amwJM (comment 3816508880) was raised on 134.007-T line 35 but the defect is owned here, so the fix is authored here once. B17 required reuse of a deferred entry captured in a PRIOR run while providing no way to FIND it: in-run reuse holds the ID the capture just returned, and across runs that handle does not exist, so the no-duplicate rule was unenforceable in exactly the case that produces duplicates. Added two criteria: DEFERRED-ENTRY DISCOVERY (lookup sources = active and archived stash plus task/run/closure residual-risk records; stable join keys = deferred entry ID when cited, else the source-ref tuple; deterministic disposition = reuse the single match, cite it, do not re-capture) and DISCOVERY FAIL-SAFE. The fail-safe is deliberately ASYMMETRIC: an ambiguous match fails CLOSED (no entry, cite all candidates, defer to Stage), while an unavailable lookup CAPTURES — because a duplicate is recoverable through 134.008-T reconciliation and a dropped finding is not. One shared default would be wrong for one of the two directions. Also carries the C4 active-cycle boundary annotation on Stop-Conditions (thread PRRT_kwDORzpWpM6amwIa).

PR #372 review-fix cycle 3 (P1-1). DISCOVERY FAIL-SAFE rewritten: both discovery-failure paths now CAPTURE unconditionally. The prior ambiguous/unconfirmed direction suppressed capture on the false ground that the finding was "provably already captured" -- false whenever a single candidate's expansion statement cannot be confirmed to describe the same expansion, which drops the finding silently. Paths now differ only in the evidence token recorded (DISCOVERY-STATUS: AMBIGUOUS with every candidate ID, or DISCOVERY-STATUS: LOOKUP-UNAVAILABLE), written inside field (2) of the fixed six-field payload -- no seventh field. Fail-closed moved from the CAPTURE decision to the IDENTITY decision. Clause (iii) replaced with a complete four-case truth table over (candidate count x identity confirmation); positive confirmation is now a required predicate for reuse.
